title: Kansas City Pulled Pork Sandwiches
seoTitle: Kansas City Pulled Pork Sandwiches | Firehall BBQ
shortDescription: KC-style pull that holds hot and builds sandwiches fast
subtitle: Sweet-smoky shoulder, thick BBQ sauce, and soft buns for ten
description: Adapted from classic Kansas City pulled pork tradition (Amazing Ribs, Meat Church): pork shoulder smokes with a balanced sweet rub, gets pulled into juices, and served with thick tomato-molasses BBQ sauce on soft buns.

steps.title: Season the shoulder
steps.instruction: Coat shoulder with mustard binder. Mix salt, brown sugar, paprika, garlic, and onion powder; rub all over. Rest 20 minutes while smoker heats to 250°F.

steps.title: Smoke low
steps.instruction: Smoke shoulder fat-side up at 250°F until bark is dark and internal temp hits 165°F, about 5–6 hours.

steps.title: Build KC sauce
steps.instruction: Simmer ketchup, molasses, vinegar, and Worcestershire 10 minutes until thick. Reserve 1 cup for finishing; rest for pulling.

steps.title: Wrap and finish
steps.instruction: Wrap tightly in foil. Continue at 250°F (or 275°F oven) until probe slides like butter and internal temp is 203°F, about 2–3 hours.

steps.title: Rest and pull
steps.instruction: Rest wrapped 45 minutes. Pour juices into a pan. Pull pork, discarding large fat. Stir in juices and KC sauce to taste.

steps.title: 170°F hold
steps.instruction: Transfer pulled pork to hotel pan, cover with foil, hold at 170°F until service. Stir in extra sauce if surface dries.

steps.title: Tonight's board
steps.instruction: Pulled pork pan with ladle, buns, slaw, and extra sauce. Build-your-own sandwich line.

steps.title: Leftovers
steps.instruction: Reheat covered with splash of water or sauce at 325°F until 165°F. Use in nachos or loaded potatoes.

proTips: 203°F is the pull temp—don't stop at 190°F or you'll fight the shoulder.
Mix slaw into the sandwich for classic KC crunch.
Finishing sauce after pulling keeps flavor bright without cooking off vinegar.
tonightSpread: Pulled pork in a hotel pan with ladle.
Buns, slaw, pickles, and extra KC sauce on the side.
leftovers: Pulled pork quesadillas with pepper jack.
BBQ pork fried rice with scallions.
whyCrewsLikeIt: KC sauce is crowd-pleasing and forgiving. Pulled pork holds covered at 170°F for hours and the sandwich line moves fast.
mealPrepNotes: Start early shift. Once pulled, hold covered at 170°F with a ladle of sauce and drippings for up to 2 hours. Wrap earlier if the smoker schedule slips.
